newsitem.title: USA: U.S. settles Nazi deportation case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. settles Nazi deportation case.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department said on Tuesday it has settled a deportation case involving a New Jersey man who has been stripped of his U.S. citizenship because of his Nazi propaganda activities in the 1940s.

It announced the settlement with Ferenc Koreh, who admitted he could be deported for assisting in Nazi-persecution during the Second World War and for lying about his wartime activities in entering the United States in 1950.

Although he agreed to the entry of a deportation order, the Justice Department said it would not seek to remove Koreh, 87, of Englewood, New Jersey, from the country without an improvement in his rapidly deteriorating health.
Department officials said Koreh was editor of a provincial newspaper in Hungary from 1941 through 1944, serving as a propagandist for the Nazis in advocating the persecution of Jews.
Koreh, a retired producer and broadcaster for Radio Free Europe, was stripped of his U.S. citizenship in 1994, and the Justice Department began deportation proceedings against him last April.

Under the settlement reached last week, Koreh did not contest that he was editor of the anti-Semitic newspaper and that he was responsible for some of the 200 racist articles which helped create a climate for Nazi persecution of Jews.
